geeklist.title: BGG.CON Virtual Flea Market 2024
geeklist.description:
[center][COLOR=#009933][size=18][b] Welcome to this year's BGG.CON Virtual Flea Market 2024![/b][/size][/COLOR][/center]
[center][size=14][b]BGG.CON 2024 VFM Table Assignments!![/b][/size][/center] [b]FINAL Version 24. Unless he world collapses, I do not want to change this![/b] [imageid=8521914 large]
[center][size=14][b]PLEASE READ THIS ENTIRE DESCRIPTION UNDER ITEM 1 RULES!![/b][/size][/center] Since this Geeklist will get very long, all the Rules of the BGG.CON Virtual Flea Market 2024 are under the first game on the first page. You are required to read and understand the requirements. This geeklist header will only have final updates so that a long header will not load for every page that people load: [listitem=11060964]Participation Requirements[/listitem]
[center][size=18]Introduction![/size][/center] Here is the concept - For people who are travelling to the convention, sellers only want to bring games that they have sold. Buyers want to plan how much space they need to bring games home. Enter the Virtual Flea Market. If you have items that you'd like to sell at BGG.Con, list them here with the condition of your items, and the price or terms (Auction, Buy it now, whatever) you'd like to sell for. Buyers settle on a price with the seller. At the con, [u]buyers give an envelope with pre-counted money to the seller[/u] who hands them the game! Quick, easy, and 4000 games exchange hands in one hour! Note that the Virtual Flea Market is different from the Math Trade and different from the BGG.CON Bazaar!
Brief Links: Need to request a game? Check out: [geeklist=342446][/geeklist] Want to search the VFM for BGG.Con 2024 GeekList? • [url=https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/342440]Eric Bettan's alphabetical search tool hereEric Bettan's alphabetical search tool here[/url] *[url=https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l=342440&mode=9&sort=0]David Rathbun's Updated search tool here[/url]
Read The first listed game for the full participation requirements: [listitem=11060964]Participation Requirements[/listitem]
.

I know there have been some etiquette discussions over the last few VFMs -- so just to put this out there -- I am always happy to entertain offers on anything listed -- so offer away on my listings!
Show me the evidence that I'm priced to the moon and need to be brought back to earth -- Shatter my dreams of a used board game funded early retirement!

[q="notacceptable406"] Show me the evidence that I'm priced to the moon and need to be brought back to earth -- Shatter my dreams of a used board game funded early retirement! [/q]
I always just hope to cover my VFM purchases + con ticket, but yes 🙂 I price my games based on the cheapest options in the BGG marketplace, but I still consider offers (and it looks like I've actually taken a below asking price offer for 6 of the 7 games I've sold thus far...normally I'd wait until October before coming down in price but it's been a slow year)

There are always people that: 1) make extreme lowball offers because it costs them nothing to do it and some people don't care about the price or need money so they take it. 2) there are always people that price high because they value the game at that price or they really just dont want to sell the game. 3) I've always found that about 1/3 of sellers are dumping games and its a great deal, 1/3 price their games over market value, and the remaining 1/3 prices it within $5 of the market value. I think part of this is people look at game x. It sold for say $30 on the marketplace but the buyer had to add 12-15 in shipping. So they paid 42-45. So some sellers price their games below 30 to sell them quick, some price close to 30 since thats what it recently sold for, and others go well someone paid 40+ due to shipping so I should be able to get that.
As a buyer I have paid slightly less than the OLGS price for a NIS copy of a game that is a recent hotness item and I've also haggled on sub $10 games to get that extra 1-3 off because that little bit adds up when you buy a lot of games.
When I do my pricing I generally look at the most recent 3-5 sales and calculate an average price based on that (removing outliers) and thats the price i list on my spreadsheet. As I dont update my spreadsheet all the time it means sometimes Im selling for a higher price as the market has declined and other times Im selling for a lower price as the game has gone up since i last priced. I'm always willing to look at the current market though and see re-evaluate. Unless i just want to dump a game though I rarely accept a low ball offer thats way off the mark of the market value. (if I have a game priced at 30 and you offer me 15 i can guarantee I'm going to say no or just ignore the offer.

I'd have to agree with you, La Donn.
As a seller, I mostly price close to the low price on the marketplace (and I don't consider shipping) so that if you buy from me, you're getting a good price (which makes it worth getting the game in Texas instead of just ordering it online). There will always be some that I don't care about that much and will take low offers because I just want to be rid of them (like Bohnanza this year) and others where I don't necessarily feel the need to own them any longer but I'd rather keep them than sell them cheap (like Final Girl this year). I'll mostly just flat decline extreme lowball offers.
As a buyer, I don't really have much in the way of "must have" games - if it's something I -really- want that's not brand new, it's probably already in my collection. So most of the time, if I can't get a significant discount off new, I probably just won't bother. Which means that if a game is listed for significantly more than I want to pay I'll just ignore it, and if it's reasonably close I'll either just buy it (if I think it's likely someone else will take it otherwise) or make an offer. This year the games I've bought have been close enough to what I wanted to pay that I've mostly just grabbed what I want without haggling.

I am just a small seller making shelf space but i use market place and ebay to price my games. But always willing to offer can always say no. But i am just trying to break even or come out ahead. I also try to judge on what other people has listed them as and go from there. If i wanna get rid of a game i am more willing to take a lowball offer if i am iffy i will wait on a lowball offer

[user=Larva_the_shinma][/user] pretty much summarized my games and approach. 🙂
I have some that I try to price roughly at the low point of the Marketplace, and I'm pretty open to offers as I'd like the space and they may go to Goodwill or a trash can. But I usually wait until October before dropping games that are easy to trade or easier to sell elsewhere.
I have some games that I really like, but I'm trying to clear some space and something has to go. I usually price those a little closer to OLGS price, just because I'm totally OK holding onto them. Then I get more aggressive in late October or early November if I know I need more space.
On the buying side, I have some that are hard to find and I'm comfortable paying whatever a current rate is. And I have some that I have some nostalgia for or want to take a shot at playing them with my kids, so I make lowball offers knowing that it's completely fine if people decline.

[user=Larva_the_shinma][/user] bout hit the nail on the head for me. I did my best to price close to what I was seeing via the Marketplace ( a couple may be a hair higher, but I am also holding hope it stays home). But I can say I have already watched one fly the coup that I was not expecting to leave so soon. LoL.
I have never been the greatest at the pricing game. But I do try to be considerate of listening to offers, and always go back and look to see if the offer is because I was overshooting by mistake. Only once did I not check so far, But I also am sitting right on your Reason #2 with it. Gonna have to, as the old Texas saying goes, Come and Take It!

I buy of lot of games so I have to watch what I spend closely. Sometimes I see a game I'm interested in and think, "I'd buy that right away if it were X price," so I offer X price. If the answer is no, I either move on or add it to a list of games to consider (raising my offer depends on what else I buy).
I sometimes worry that I'm insulting or wasting the time of the seller, and I don't want to come across as a skinflint, but unless the seller states that the price is firm, I will assume they welcome all reasonable offers. Most sellers are cordial but a few seem to get cranky with lowballs.

roger, my assumption is most sellers don't get offended unless its a true lowball offer. There are a handful of users that throw out a bunch of subpar offers off the hope that someone accepts them. Typically i get these type of offers from 2-3 people each year. The typical offer they make is 50% or more off my asking price. I get why they do it, some people just dont care about the games and any offer is better than keeping the game. Other people need the money so for them just getting something is better than nothing.
I used to buy 100-150 games per year off the VFM typically I'd make offers in the range of $15 game, offer between 10-12, $10 game offer 7-8, $20 game offer 15, but in general I never really tried for more than 5 off a game unless it was a much higher priced item or if i was interested but wasnt really interested or if i saw something i wanted and the asking price seemed outside of the range of what the game sold for. (such as someone asking $50 for a game that the average sale price on the market was 30ish)
Now I i know some sellers get offended when offers are made and others don't. One thing i would generally do when i thought my offer might sound insulting would be to send a PM explaining my offer and make my offer that way so other potential buyers wouldnt be turned off from the item.

Yeah I go back and forth on what I want to do. In the past, I would make offers based on quantity over quality. So I was looking for good deals on subpar games. As a seller, I am okay with entertaining any offer. If its too low, I will probably just pass on that offer. Some games I would rather keep in my collection for the price that was offered and some I am willing to let go for a much cheaper price than the marketplace. Really just depends on the game and price.

The dumb thing is, for some the offers, it practically costs me as much to get the game to Texas as I'd be getting for it, so I'd be better off just dropping it off at Goodwill and being done with it. But I still might take them just because it ensures I sell enough to have a table, which means I don't have to arrange meetup times to hand off the more expensive games.
Yeah it really depends on how you are going about getting them to Texas. Are you flying in or driving? I just take my minivan and load it up each year, so bringing a $5 game isn't an issue here.

[q="PumpkinGirl"]This is my first con and my first VFM. We've seen a fair amount of sales these past few days, but the con is still 2 months out. Sellers, do most people follow through with buying what they say they will?[/q] In general, yes. I’ve sold for many years and rarely had a sale fall through.

as a buyer and seller:
Buyer: I've only had 3 sellers back out of/forget to pack a game i bought.
Seller: I've had a grand total of 4-5 people who didnt show up to buy a game, or got there and went "I thought this game was X that had a similar name. That being said I'm also guilty of having the occasional issue with a game im selling. One year a pipe burst and one of the boxes of games I was selling was on the floor, so I sent a geekmail to everyone letting them know I was canceling that sale because the games went from the condition i said to damaged. I have also had an issue before where my spread sheet still had a game on it I had sold the previous year and I didn't catch it and posted the game and when I went to pull it it was no where to be found.
Will mention there seems to be some law in the universe that states "The person buying your $3 card game will only show up 1 minute before the VFM closes." :)

I have only had one buyer "no show" in all of the VFM events where I have sold games. I was later able to sell the item they were supposed to pick up for a higher price, so win for me. 🙂 As a first time buyer (or seller) the best tip is to be organized! Know what you're buying, for how much, and from who (whom?). Try to be efficient and walk from one end of the ball room to the other so you don't have to back track. Most of the transactions seem to take place in the first 30 minutes of the 1 hour reserved for this event.
This will be only my second time to the Con, but my first time all my sales were squared away before we even got to the meet-up. That's a lot less likely if someone is moving a LOT of games though.

People will follow though at least my experiences as a buyer and seller now the buyer might show up at very end of the hour but you are waiting around. I myself am buying alot less this year and selling a bunch more am also gonna get a table at the fm. But i never had any issues not getting my stuff for the price over the years

When I sell games I expect negotiating between the buyer until they meet their Max or I meet my minimum. Low ball offers are fine. I usually ignore them. As a buyer I subscribe games I want to look at again and wait for them to drop unless I really want it and I will put a bid. Sometimes, I wait for the prices to drop and get a deal or hope someone buys it before I fully commit. 😆

I think everyone just has their reasons for the offers they make. I want to purchase for as little as possible, because I know for the most part I am still going to lose money when I resell. The lower I can get it, the less I will lose in the future. Some games that I make lower offers for are ones that I am interested in playing, but not sure how long on the shelf of shame it will sit. Lower prices for me is lower risk in the future. I am trying to change what I buy this year to only stuff that I know will get played in the first 6 months.
Also, I am looking to buy cheap stuff that is new in shrink as I host 2 smaller retreats of about 20 people and enjoy giving everyone a free game.

I'll sold quite a few games at both the bazaar and the VFM, so I know how much work it is to deal with the logistics and lug big boxes of games to the con. I applaud the organizers and everyone who participates. Although I try to make my BGG.con not about acquisition, the VFM for me is one of the highlights of the con that I can start enjoying in September!
I usually try to offer something reasonable that Im willing to buy - negotiations is part of the game. if i don't get the deal - that's fine - i'll just wait for the next one.

I sold about 30 & bought 330 games last year (some for me personally but 319 for the US Navy mission -GREAT SUCCESS BTW THANK ALL OF YOU WHO DONATED OR SOLD GAMES TO ME!!) and my roomie & I split the room so that we could run & pick up buys easier by staying on one side of the room. We also tried our best to meet up outside the VFM around the hotel to get as many buys/sells done beforehand, It was a mad house but we got it ALL done in that VFM hour! 🎉🎉🎉 Organization & communication with buyers/sellers is the key!

Hey folks, I have been meaning to rework the design behind my index / list tool for about a year, and just haven't dedicated the time. When lists like this get big, BGG isn't super efficient and sending the list data when requested. It looks like the "yulgames" version of the indexing tool has already converted to a scheduled or cached retrieval (I am assuming this because when I go to their site it says "list updated X minutes ago" rather than showing live). I am going to take my version of the list offline until I can rework it using plans I set up a while ago. So until further notice, the Geek List index hosted at sunderedrealm.com will be offline. At least there's another option already in place. 🙂
Thanks for the work on this Dave.

I try and sell my stuff for the lowest prices I can according to condition. There maybe be cheaper prices but they are for good or vg and mine might be NIS or a Kickstarter Version or have geek bits in it or lots of exp or promos. I don't mind asking for lower but I probably will say no until it gets closer to the con, not right after i put stuff up for the most part. Unless someone on here has sold the same game in the same condition for a lower price then I will probably meet it. I look at the geek market, noble knight games and other stores to set my prices. If it is high i may want to keep it or could not find a price and did not know what to price it at . I have a few games like that , only 1 or two where that comes into effect , 1 is Valda where i had the grand master pledge with the cherry wooden box and it does not come up and it was an expensive pledge. I know I will probably end up keeping that one. But you never know. I am not in a big hurry to sell this year because I only have so much space as I downsized my car after an accident. So if you see something majorly overpriced , give me a yell. And same with something majorly underpriced but that will have probably already been sold. lol.

This is by far one of my favorite events of the convention. It is well run and lot's of fun. Thank you [user=Solamar][/user] in the Fall and [user=Tolio][/user] in the Spring along with all of the folks who participate to make this happen. :meeple:
I rarely buy games at full price these days. There's an oversaturated market with people who had collections of 100 games prior to 2020 easily having double or triple (or more if we are honest 😆) games now. I'd imagine most of us could agree we have too many games and not enough time to play all of them.
As a [b]Seller[/b] I'm happy to sell the games I list on the VFM at reasonable/comparable prices and some of them at really great deals. I often will lower prices as we get closer to the convention. I'd rather have some cash to help pay for my purchases than more boxes sitting on my shelves. I will sometimes mule some games for people in my game group [url=https://www.facebook.com/groups/FortWorthGameNight]Fort Worth Game Night Community[/url].
As a [b]Buyer[/b] I am looking for good deals or specific games (sometimes for friends) on the VFM. To me, I'm trying to get better deals than what's on BGG Marketplae or on Facebook buy/sell/trade board game groups. Sometimes I'm picking up games or selling for my game group. Still others I'm looking for New in Shrink games to giveaway at our 3 day convention [url=https://tabletop.events/conventions/geek-game-days-2025/badgetypes]Geek Game Days[/url] (About 500 people) in Arlington, Tx typically held 1st or 2nd week in August.
Here’s what I typically expect as far as pricing goes both as a buyer and seller.
• [b]eBay[/b] - Highest • [b]FLGS[/b] (Friendly Local Game Stores) - 2nd Highest (unless there's some type of rewards, Buy 2 Get One Free, or BOGO... When I'm buying here I'm supporting local business.) • [b]Online Retailers - [/b]Amazon, CoolStuffInc, GameNerdz, MiniatureMarket, etc. - 3rd Highest • [b]BoardGameGeek Marketplace - [/b]4th Highest, Price History is good comparison tool • [b]National/International Buy, Sell, Trade Game Groups on Facebook - [/b] 5th Highest • [b]Local Buy, Sell, Trade Game Groups on Facebook[/b] - 6th Highest • [b]Virtual Flea Markets [/b](BGG.Spring in May, Geek Game Days in August, or BGG.Con in November, ): 2nd Cheapest - 30-50%+ off retail or more • [b]Bazaar[/b] (Selling on the spot typically with cash at a convention) - Cheapest (Better deals than on the VFM)

I agree, this is the part of the con that happens before the con...I'm having fun watching for stuff I want to come up, even though there's not necessarily anything in particular I was planning to buy this year :-)

the VFM has always been my favorite event at BGG con. The chaotic hustle of trying to gather all of my purchases and the high energy in the room. It kind of makes me sad though that I don't have many non-new release games that I'm actively looking for these days.
Yeah, a friend of mine always picks up my purchases because I'm selling, and I gotta say, he definitely has the fun part of it :-)

Yeah - if you do not have too much to get you can get some done. It's better to have a runner for that though if able.

Once Solamar makes the list live there is an easy way to add items to the VFM geeklist, courtesy of Eric Bettan (Carnage994):
[size=13][u][b]Instructions on Adding Games[/b][/u] 1. Add all your items to your BGG games collection list. 2. Tag items [b]for sale[/b] in your BGG collection by labelling them as "For Trade", [u]Note: This won't include expansions at this time.[/u] 3. Then use [geekurl=/geekgold/transfer/user/Carnage994]Eric Bettan[/geekurl]'s (feel free to tip him) posting tool with instructions to add games: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/342440 4. Type in your BGG [b]Username[/b] and click [b]load[/b]. 5. Your "For Trade" list will be populated. 6. Simply add notes to the field that says [b]"Message to add on each entry"[/b] for example:[/size]
[i]"----- Additional Notes: 1. Pickup locally near west side of Fort Worth. Otherwise let's meet up at the VFM Thursday from 7pm to 8pm. 2. I accept Cash, Paypal, Zelle, or Venmo. 3. If you are providing cash please bring exact change in an envelope. 4. Open to discounts on multiple game buys. Make me an offer! Please post here and/or send a Geekmail with any questions."[/i]
[size=13]7. In the "Buy it now" field enter the price of the game. 8. Then Click "[b]Add Item[/b]". 9. Rinse, wash, and repeat. [/size]

[q="kristernevin"]If you do the mark as sold on each game it updates the price history properly.[/q]
Or maybe incorrectly updates the price history, devaluing the game and hindering all future sales of that game. For example, there's [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/geeklist/342440/bggcon-virtual-flea-market-2024?itemid=11150805#11150805]an item that was traded marked sold for $1.00[/url] in this VFM. That item's price history now shows the latest sale at $1.00 when the item was actually traded. The deeply discounted "get it off my shelves" sales at the BGG.con Bazaar don't end up in the price history - so why make that happen here? Also, pushing that button adds to your bill at BGG before you've completed the sale. I've no problem totaling sales and giving BGG their cut, I really just don't like what it does to the secondary game market when that button is used to do it.

The reason you would not do it is that if someone does not pick up the game and you marked as sold you are on the hook for items you did not actually sell. This happened to me when the SOLD button first appeared. It also triggers you to pay fees before the con even comes since we start the VFM so much in advance.

Hi, folks, I am happy to share that I have finally had the time to rework my search index (hosted at Sundered Realm). If that's all you want to know, stop reading. 🙂
https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l=342440
The reason I reworked it was because once a Geek List gets over about 1000 entries things start to really slow down. I was getting really frustrated when I would go to my page and have to refresh over and over because of time out messages. So I changed the way my index works. At this point it refreshes only in the background and a cache (store) a copy of the list on my server. That means when you go to the page it responds immediately (or at least very fast) rather than waiting for BGG to serve the list. It also means that if items get deleted here on BGG I still have - at least in theory - a record of them on my server, so I can help the list owners educate folks about deleting items.
It also means that I can add new features, like the ability to sort / track different things. I have also added a search box at the top. The primary use of the index was to allow users to use their browser search function to look for a game...now you can enter all or part of a game name in the search box and it will filter the list down for you. I found that to be much easier than using the browser search where results might be spread out over multiple different sections. Now if you - for example - search for "dragon" then all games (and only games) with the word dragon in them will show up. 🙂
I have a few more things I want to do, but I am ready for folks to start using the list again. Please send bug reports via Geek Mail if needed. Thanks!

Hi, folks, I was looking at the list index results this morning. I think typically there are about 60 seller tables at this event? Right now the cutoff for the top 60 sellers is 10 items. In the past I think they have also combined two smaller sellers onto a single table to allow more than 60 sellers to officially participate. I thought I would talk briefly about how my index tool detects sold items. It's an imprecise process. 🙂
Option 1 is the most reliable and happens when a seller uses the "Mark Sold" button on their item. That's about as official / concrete as it can get. When I retrieve the list data those items have a sold tag, the actual sold amount, and the currency value. Anything that is marked in this way is absolutely confirmed as sold.
Option 2 is also reliable for marking an item sold but the price detection is imprecise, and that's when a seller uses the +sold+ tag somewhere in their listing. The +sold+ tag predates the availability of the "Mark Sold" option on a Geek List item, and many sellers prefer to use this rather than use the button because of flexibility. (Buyers may back out, may no-show at the event, etc.). I personally use this option when marking my items sold.
Option 3 is much less precise. It involves looking for the word "sold" without the + tags on either side anywhere in a listing. This can be highly problematic as people can randomly use the word in a sentence (this was sold recently for $20 so I am listing for $10) or the letters can appear in a word (soldier). So my current logic is to check for the word "sold" and then also check to see if the body of the listing has a user tag [ username = ] somewhere. That would imply that the listing is sold to that user, and it's counted as sold. If the word "sold" appears but there is no user tag, then the item is considered not sold. I noticed several examples of this while scanning the list this week while working on my code, but don't have a specific link. My tool is smart enough to ignore the letters embedded in another word (like soldier) now.
I can't comment on exactly how the YulGame list tags items as sold, but that's how my index works.
Bottom line - if you want to get credit for items being sold to try to qualify for a table, please either use the [b]Mark Sold[/b] button or the [b]+sold+[/b] tag somewhere in your listing. Those are the two most reliable methods that we have to identify sold items.
Thanks!

Hi, folks, a quick update on my Geek List search / index tool. I have added a feature that is going to be useless for mobile users (sorry!) but if you're on a computer you can hover your mouse over a link and get a preview of the listing here on BGG. I added that because it helps me understand why one item might be price higher than another item even though they're the same game. For example, one might be new in shrink and the other opened, or one might include some expansions. The post preview only shows the first 250-ish characters of the post so if the text is longer it won't show up.
I have added a search field at the top of the screen which is 95% functional but still has some quirks that I plan to fix...for example, it doesn't always remember your other search settings (such as All versus New versus Sold game status). I found the search field to be helpful as you can filter the entire list down to just the games you want, versus using the search/find feature in your browser. No wild cards are required, just enter the text you want to search for.
I have been talking to the author of the Yulgames index tool. We treat some of the data differently. 🙂 I look for tags with the + sign ([c]+sold+[/c] and [c]+remove+[/c]) and he does not. He parses the text to identify the buyer, and I (currently) do not. We both acknowledge the +altname+ tag but use it differently. He uses the key word "withdrawn" to remove an item, and I do not currently do that but plan to add it so our tools get more consistent. My method for the VFM and the Math Trade as been this: Post games on both lists. If a game sells, then I submit an empty list on the trade. Once I post my want list for the trade, which I do at the last possible chance, if I get an offer, I explain it is in the trade and will finalize the transaction later. They are free to withdraw the offer. After the trade, if the game is traded, I post the new status on the VFM.
Never had a problem, mainly because I post on the VFM early enough that my games have been on the VFM for 3+ weeks prior to the Math Trade.
Sadly, this may all be moot because I feel the VFM is killing the Math Trade.

Just in case anybody is still subscribed to this geeklist, the BGG 2025 Math Trade is up! This year the math trade is concluding early, [i]before[/i] the 2025 VFM! That means everyone will know what traded and what didn't, and there will be no interference or issues with games cross selling/trading. If you don't know what a math trade is or know but have been too confused or afraid to try it, post in the discussion thread and someone can help you. It's a no-risk way to trade games and conventions are the best place for it since there's no shipping!
[thread=3570265]BGG Con 2025 Math Trade![/thread]

item.body:
[center][COLOR=#009933][size=18][b] Welcome to this year's BGG.CON Virtual Flea Market 2024[/b][/size][/COLOR] [size=14][b]PLEASE READ THIS ENTIRE HEADER!![/b][/size][/center] [u][b]Introduction[/b][/u] Here is the concept - For people who are travelling to the convention, sellers only want to bring games that they have sold. Buyers want to plan how much space they need to bring games home. Enter the Virtual Flea Market. If you have items that you'd like to sell at BGG.Con, list them here with the condition of your items, and the price or terms (But it now, Auction (Must have a stated end date and close as SOLD at least 1 week before event.), whatever) you'd like to sell for. Buyers settle on a price with the seller. At the con, [u]buyers give an envelope with pre-counted money to the seller[/u] who hands them the game! Quick, easy, and 4000 games exchange hands in one hour! Note that the Virtual Flea Market is different from the Math Trade and different from the BGG.CON Bazaar!
[b]Coordination:[/b] I (Sterling Babcock, Solamar) will be running the Virtual Flea Market and attending. My wife, Marcia (RedPhoenixNia) will also be helping me as well as Team Geek.
[b]Date & Location: [/b] Held in Reunion EFGH Thursday evening (6p-7p VFM Seller Setup, 7p-8p VFM). Enter from the 3 doors in the hall. * Please send your [b]thanks to Jeff Anderson[/b] and the BGG.CON team for continuing to allow us to have the VFM for BGG.CON! * Please be [b]polite and courteous[/b] in all your communication. * We won't be requiring masks but [u]we do recommend masks in this crowded situation[/u]. Please remember the general Health & Safety Guidelines: "Respect the personal choices of those around you. [b]We will not tolerate harassment of any kind[/b], and this includes the choice to wear or not wear a mask."
[u][b]Room Plan[/b][/u] [center]< To Be Posted the final week before BGG.CON >[/center] This year the room plan will be slightly different. Because of limited space it was very difficult to give everyone a table and keep the order alphabetically. The tables will continue to be [b]listed by BGG username[/b] in [u]approximate[/u] alphabetical order. However, [u]sellers will be rearranged a bit out of order[/u] to facilitate dividing up the tables by number of games sold. As seen last year, there will be an alphabetical list of sellers at the door which will indicate the exact row and column of a particular sellers table. For example Solamar may be at table G5. That way, [b]you can look up who you are purchasing from ahead of time, and mark them on your purchase envelopes AHEAD OF TIME[/b]. That will help you find the seller quickly and efficiently. There are no guarantee that every seller will be able to get a table, but we hope to have part of a table available for everyone that sells 10 or more games, based on participation. I will have signs on the tables so it is easy to see them. See [url=https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Stats/342440]https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Stats/342440[/url] for the list of sold items.
[b]Please, please, please be patient and help others. We have to make sure this goes smoothly so that we do not get restricted in the future. This is the largest VFM ever! [/b]
Here are the assignments: Image to be added. For an example, see the SECOND IMAGE in the OLD 2023 BGG.con example at: [geeklist=321725][/geeklist]
[u][b]Seller Guidelines[/b][/u] * [b]All sellers MUST be BGG.CON attendees to participate in the virtual flea market[/b]. Team Geek will be at the doors to enforce this, and buyers should not purchase from sellers who are not attending BGG.CON. * There are 80 tables. There will be no ticket to sign up for sellers tables. I will assign a table to each seller up to our capacity. (e.g. if you sell approximately 10 games or more you will get a table. If you do not get a ticket because you sold too few games, you are on your own to arrange the exchange with the buyer. Any auctions must have a stated end date and close as SOLD 1 week prior to the event or they do not qualify for a table assignment. * You are expected to [u]be at your sellers table for the full hour[/u] or until all your games are sold. If you also want to be a buyer, make other time arrangements to do your pickups outside the VFW event, or have another person do your pickups during the VFW. You must remain at your sellers table. * Anyone with a BGG.CON badge may participate in the VFM. If you do not plan to attend the VFM for pickup, make that clear to your buyers in your listing. * [b]The tables in the room will be arranged by the sellers BGG username. [/b] * [b][u]Do NOT delete your item[/u].[/b] People expect the geek list numbers not to change. If you remove an item, Mark them as sold or no longer available. * Please do add your items to this list! You choose how to sell your items: Fixed Price, Auction, Dutch Auction. You should monitor your own items. Any auctions must have a stated end date and close as SOLD 1 week prior to the event or they do not qualify for a table assignment. * Sellers: List Aggregator Tools: - If your item is an auction, please include the word "[b]Auction[/b]" someplace. (It helps the aggregator tools) - If you are selling an item that deserves an [b]alternate name[/b] in a summary list (i.e. Misc Game Accessory), please place this code in your item someplace: "+altname+ Whatever You'd Like To Call Your Item -altname-" - [u]Mark sold items as: [b]SOLD[/b] so that the summary tools[/u] can remove it from the available list. Mark who purchased it as well. See also using +sold+ - If you change your price, [u]please keep the new price on the same line of the geeklist[/u] (Do something like $25 $20) * There is an [u]easy way to add items[/u] to the geeklist, courtesy of Eric Bettan (Carnage994): Alphabetical search tool: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/342440 The link to add games is: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/342440 * Sellers with tickets will be allowed into the room to set up between 6-6:45pm on Thursday evening. No games will be allowed into the room after 6:45 pm. Sellers stay on INSIDE of tables. Do NOT block the outside traffic with games! * You [u]may NOT use hotel luggage carts[/u]. * Please open all your envelopes and collect the cash before disposing of the envelope! * Sellers should arrange a bulk commission at the BGG Marketplace * Any attempt by a seller to deceive a buyer by significantly miss describing the item (e.g. missing stated expansion) will be dealt with harshly. * Sellers need to make sure that they do not sell the same game twice or trade and sell. If you do that, then you need to carry through with both transactions by obtaining another copy of the game. Either that, or you need to come to an agreement with both parties, possibly compensating one party for the error. Do not list a game in the VFM and the math trade at the same time. * Please be kind, bring a sign, and try to help each other out.
[u][b]Tips from Past Sellers[/b][/u]: 1. Create a spreadsheet with the games you're selling. Create columns for Game Name, Game Cost, Method of Payment, Buyer Name, Buyer BGG Name, Buyer Table Assignment, Comments, etc. If you’re paying via PayPal, Venmo, etc. make a note. Print off your list prior to the event and bring it with you. 2. Send out geek mails and confirm with the game sale with people who have bought games from you. Sometimes people miss responses to game transactions. 3. Have a full-length, printed sheet with your Tabletop.events Name, BGG User Name, and Avatar/Logo on it for people to find you more easily. 4. Print out the table assignments beforehand. Circle your table. 5. Removable Sticky notes on the game with the name of the Buyer picking up your games would be helpful. 6. Please [u]get your money out of the envelopes[/u] and deposit the empty envelopes in the trash. Please do not leave it for staff to clean up!
[center][size=14][b]Not following through with commitments[/b][/size][/center] I really hate that I have to post this. Unfortunately, there are too many sellers/buyers backing out of deals this year, and it is taking an inordinate amount of time. The VFM is just so big that we cannot hand hold both sides to get them to communicate and resolve issues. [b]Sellers must have their games to sell before they list them. Buyers must follow through with commitments which they made months ago. If something unexpected comes up both need to come to some sort of mutual agreement and perhaps compensation.[/b] Both sides should also notify me of the resolution. If this is not done, I will unfortunately have to ban some users from future participation in the virtual flea market. If you are contacted by me in geekmail, you need to respond immediatly and work things out with the other party to mutual agreement. (This is a very small minority, so if you have not already been contacted by me, then it is not you.)
[u][b]Buyers Guidelines[/b][/u] * You may not enter before 7 pm. PLEASE BE PROMPT at 7 pm!! We have to be clear of the room by no later than 8 pm to make room for other BGG events. * Buyers MUST attend the START of the hour of exchange and stay until all your games are received. Do NOT be late and make people wait for you! Buyers are REQUIRED to either show up, or notify the Seller they will not be there. Do NOT be 'that guy' which makes a seller wait all hour trying to find you. You must find the seller! * Buyers who fail to make their committed purchase will be reported to Matthew Monin (Octavian). * Buyers stay on the OUTSIDE of the tables for ease of finding games. * If you are a [b]buyer[/b], please bring one envelope for each seller you are buying from. [b]Each envelope should be marked on the outside with the seller's user name, table assignment, and the items you are buying and should contain exact change![/b] After doing this for a few years, we can tell you that this makes the event go much more smoothly for everyone. * The room will be organized according to [b]Sellers' User Names![/b] in mostly alphabetical order. Check the table assignments before hand and mark each envelope with the seller's table location! * Any attempt by a buyer to deceive the seller and pick up a game which you did not rightfully purchase will be dealt with harshly. * Failure to follow these rules may cause you to be rejected from future Virtual Flea Markets.
[u][b]Tips from Past Buyers[/b][/u]: 1. Create a spreadsheet with the games you're buying. Create columns for Game Name, Game Cost, Method of Payment, Seller Tabletop Events Name, Seller BGG Name, Comments, etc. If you're paying via PayPal, Venmo, etc. make a note. Print off your list prior to the event and bring it with you. 2. Buy plain envelopes. Write down the name of each game you’re buying and the name of the Seller. [u]Provide exact change.[/u] Put your name on your envelopes so it's easily identified as paid by sellers or in case it gets lost. 4. Bring plenty of bags to haul off your 'new' games. You won't be able to use the luggage carts.
[u][b]Expectations[/b][/u] Since this event has gotten so large (also fun and successful), we need everyone's help to keep the event organized so we can continue it in future years. Please be on time. Please be considerate to the several hundred other people that are participating so this can continue to be a great experience! There is nothing more frustrating that walking through the room looking for someone, only to find out they are running late or wandering about the hall looking for their own pickups.
[u][b]Summary of Unsold Games[/b] - Use one of these links for an alphabetized list of games still available[/u] Alphabetical search tool courtesy of Eric Bettan (Carnage994): https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/342440
Here’s another search list function by David Rathbun: https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l= 342440 (Temporarily disabled to improve efficiency)
[u][b]Request List[/b][/u] If there is something you are looking for, think about adding it to Virtual Flea Market for Delivery to BGG.Con 2024 - Request List. [geeklist=342446][/geeklist]
[u][b]Shipping Games[/u][/b]: See the BGG.CON Master list for FedEx delivery information.
[u][b]Math Trade[/b][/u] If you participate in the BGG.Con Math Trade, please make sure that items are NOT listed in both at the same time. However, this will not be monitored. So if you do so, it is your responsibility to immediately mark items sold as no longer available in the Math trade, and mark them deleted from this list if they are traded. If you make a mistake and sell a game twice, it is your responsibility to fulfill all your commitments, no matter what the cost is to you. It is far better that you avoid conflicts like this.
[u][b]BGG.CON Bazaar Marketplace[/b][/u] The BGG.CON Bazaar Marketplace is a separate event run at 10 am on Friday, where you can explore and purchase games at the con. It is not related to the Virtual Flea Market, but please do attend!
[u][b]Tuesday Night Meetup[/b][/u] BGG.Con staff has advised me that since they do not officially take any hotel space on Tuesday, there can be no official or unofficial events prior to Wednesday.
[u][b]Adding Games to the List[/b][/u] Thanks to Zafin for this! There is an easy way to add items to the VFM geeklist, courtesy of Eric Bettan (Carnage994): 1. Add all your items to your BGG games collection list. 2. Tag items [b]for sale[/b] in your BGG collection by labelling them as "For Trade". Note: This won't include expansions at this time. 3. Then use [geekurl=/geekgold/transfer/user/Carnage994]Eric Bettan[/geekurl]'s (feel free to tip him) posting tool with instructions to add games: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/342440 4. Type in your BGG [b]Username[/b] and click [b]load[/b]. 5. Your list will be populated. 6. Simply add notes to the field that says [b]"Message to add on each entry"[/b] for example: [size=9][i]"----- Additional Notes: 1. Let's meet up at the VFM Thursday from 7pm to 8pm. 2. I accept Cash, Paypal, Zelle, or Venmo. 3. If you are providing cash please bring exact change in an envelope. 4. Open to discounts on multiple game buys. Make me an offer! Please post here and/or send a Geekmail with any questions."[/i][/size] 7. In the "Buy it now" field enter the price of the game. 8. Then Click "[b]Add Item[/b]". 9. Rinse, wash, and repeat. BONUS here's the Eric Bettan's search tool - Alphabetical search tool: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/342440 Alternatively here's David Rathbun's updated search function: https://sunderedrealm.com/bgg/bgg-list.php?l=342440&mode=9&sort=0
[b]Using Item Tags[/b] in your listing: +altname+ Whatever You'd Like To Call Your Item -altname- +sold+ +remove+ The +altname+ tag changes your item title. The +sold+ tag avoids improperly tagging an item as sold simply because the word "sold" appears in the listing, perhaps in the game name or something. The tag +remove+ is used to remove an item from the list aggregator tools without actually deleting it from the Geek List.
Tag this item: +sold+

Joshua Says: The book is selling fast. Get it while you can, because once it's gone, it might be gone for good.

[q="Solamar"]Joshua Says: The book is selling fast. Get it while you can, because once it's gone, it might be gone for good.[/q] Unbelievable. The book has already sold out on our website. The 22 "stock" that I had available on the website as of yesterday morning was everything that I hadn't already set aside to take to Essen Spiel to be sold at the SpielBar booth during the event. And they went QUICK.
I realize that there may still be people who haven't ordered but would like to guarantee that they'll be able to receive a copy at Essen Spiel or otherwise. Looking at [listitem=11089411]the book's entry in the SPIEL '24 Most Wanted Games Tracker Geeklist[/listitem], there are currently 23 Geeks who have listed the book as a "Must Have." So, I want to make sure I at least take 23 copies with me to be sold at the booth, just in case all 23 of them will not have preordered by then. So, for now, I'll readjust the "stock" on our website to add whatever copies I have available to be sold in excess of those 23 - effective until midnight EDT on Tuesday, Sept 24th, 2024. If you want a copy and have not preordered for pickup at the fair by then, the only way to get the book will be to attend Essen Spiel in-person (or by proxy) at buy a copy directly at the SpielBar booth while supplies last.
Should there be any remaining unsold copies of the book after the fair, I'll readjust the website's stock to include them, but I wouldn't count on it.

I'm fairly sure this came from a crowdfunding campaign but I can't currently find details.
[q="wmspringer"]Not sure. Is there any easy way to tell?[/q] Honestly not sure. Let me do some digging and see if there is.

It sounds like you've removed the shrink wrap, so it should say "second edition" at the top of the rules cover. Also, I believe the map in the second edition is 2-sided.
I believe if you got it as an add-on to the 1947 KS, it is the second edition.
To be upfront with you, I am still on the fence about purchasing this one, but any buyer interested in this game will want to know which edition.
What’s the difference between editions? I bought a copy through the JVMF, so probably first edition.
Wow, that’s actually quite a bit of changes. *sigh*
I'm not in office this week (the game is in my office at work) but I'll check when I'm back.
You leave games at work. That's cool.
Every office should contain a bunch of 18xx.

I have stuff shipped to my workplace and sometimes it sits around my office for a bit before I get around to bringing it home. Alas, only stuff that plays in <20min actually gets played at the office!

item.comment: $80 is a tough ask. I'll wait till at least the start of November before dropping the price $40.
I can understand. I was basing it on the noble knight game store and what was listed at cgs website. Thanks for considering.
I'm super confused. CGS has Apocalypse Adventures at $129. Awakenings is $79. I'm now uncertain of which I have. I'll get this updated tomorrow. I'm really sorry for the confusion!

Ok, I'm going to mark this as removed, and repost. I have Apocalypse Adventures (the actual expansion), Awakenings (the stretch goal box), Lorien (the expansion elf mage), the upgrade box, and 2 of the large coins. I'm guessing that means they are sold separately at CGS, and that combined they would all go for the $200+ range. I'm now just really confused as to if CGS is selling the KS stretch goals at $80.

[B]Version:[/B] [B]Language:[/B] [B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]This is for a near complete collection of Arcadia Quest and Masmorra in excellent condition.
There are 3 missing items and two caveats to this being complete.
The missing items: The nameless campaign The Usagi Yojimbo pack and from Masmorra the monster dice set
Now for the two caveats. First, you likely notice I don't have the guildmaster or the optional extra figures from the first kickstarter. i instead have the warpaint collection. This included painted minis for every figure released for the kickstater so you have every character released just not their boxes. The only other downside to this is they did not include the game cards for any of the characters in the warpaint. However i printed out all the character's cards and sleeved them (and most of the other characters) with magic cards behind them so you can't tell the difference. I do have beyond the grave full game and all game components. I got rid of the box and combined it with the base game. Which leads me to the second caveat, i don't have the original unpainted minis for arcadia quest or beyond the grave since i had the warpaint i got rid of the unpainted minis which were pointless.
Condition wise everything is great. I never played inferno, pets, or riders campaigns so the game content in those are mostly all new. Item cards, heroes, pets, and riders were all combined though. We simply would always just play base or beyond campaigns. All content we did use was sleeved when played. There are still a good amount of figures and extras in shrink.
Masmorra was played twice
Ok now onto what i do have with the optional figures that are included in the warpaint noted.
Warpaint Basegame Warpaint Beyond the Grave Warpaint Extras & Optional Arcadia Quest Beyond the Grave Inferno Pets Riders Masmorra Plastic Coins multiple sets Metal Coins Health markers (probably 2 sets) Skull tokens All factions bags and faction plastic markers (some not pictured) Healing fountain promo extra Frosted dice (extra dice possibly too from kickstarters) Plastic game tokens - unopened Poison dragon Chaos dragon - NIS Fire Dragon - NIS Ice Dragon - NIS A whole lotta lava Hell of a Box Masmorra KS exlusive box Riders KS Exclusive box Masmorra crossover kit - NIS Masmorra Adventuers Set - NIS Masmorra promo dice set (above the ks exclusive set) Luke the Lucky Tomrick Haldor & Brenna Nibbles (in warpaint) Bob the conjurer (in warpaint) Elysia (in warpaint) Tiaret & Mittens Leeroy Aeric Farfalla Yun McHammer Hassan Anvil & Valma Zahra (in warpaint and optional extra copy) Mamba & Rosh Viola & Crash - NIS Pigsy (warpaint) Cerby Slingshot Promo cards Pet Pack 1 - NIS Princess Pearl Yona & Kuruk - NIS Hilda Pet Pack 2 - NIS Riders - Pack 2 Hoshi Nina Chuck - NIS Riders - Pack 1[/I]

This is a 2-player dueling card game. Time Division contains cards for 3 eras: [b]Ancient Egypt, Dark Ages, the 80s[/b]. You can play a single era or a campaign of 3 eras. Players try to win control over an era by gathering the most influential characters. They achieve this through the way they draft and play the character cards.

Used, excellent condition (played twice).
[-][size=14]$15[/size][/-]
Indus 2500 BCE is a flip-and-write game in which on each turn players either pick a terrain card from the market and draw the pattern as shown (including walls to protect against calamities) or reserve resources to build more advance buildings.

[size=14]$5[/size]
Crypt is a small-box set collection game with a unique dice placement mechanic for 1 to 4 players.
Place your servant dice on treasure cards, choosing any value on each die. Choosing a higher value can ward off your opponents, but it also increases the odds that your servant will become exhausted. After everyone has placed their servant dice, everyone rolls. If you roll less than your chosen value, you lose the die.

Hanayama Jigsaw 28 Puzzle
[img]https://i.ebayimg.com/images/g/v6UAAOSwig1jpHTh/s-l1200.jpg[/img]
There are way too many edge pieces and frustratingly large tabs and blanks in this 28 piece jigsaw brainteaser puzzle! An ingenious twist on the traditional jigsaw puzzle, the Jigsaw 28 is actually a challenging packing puzzle that will have you scratching your head.
Yuu Asaka has created a line of creative packing-style puzzles that have taken the puzzle world by storm. They all share solutions with an absolutely captivating twist, Try it out and see why Yuu's inventive packing puzzles have become a sensation! A fantastic puzzle to share with friends!
There is only one solution. Tray measures 10 cm x 10 cm.
Comes in the solved state inside a plastic ziploc bag with Japanese writing. Designed by Yuu Asaka and produced by Hanayama.
[b]Condition:[/b] Like New [b]BIN: [/b] $15.00

Double Jigsaw Puzzle
[img]https://cdn.cybassets.com/s/files/8032/ckeditor/pictures/content_a9e31a6a-7cce-4642-98f5-46a26deb905c.jpg[/img]
[img]https://cdn.cybassets.com/s/files/8032/ckeditor/pictures/content_16ad9f99-d8ad-4a88-9e3b-32b1be943d22.jpg[/img]
Put all six puzzle pieces into the frame. The first layer of the puzzle must be inside the frame, and the second layer can extend beyond the frame. The puzzle cannot be stacked to the third layer.
3/5 difficulty rating

Thank you for checking, I really didn't want another incomplete set and the two versions I have the cards are different sizes so I couldn't merge them. I have a huge supply of cardboard coins, no big issue for me. Mark me as sold, I have an envelope with $20 in it on my bookshelf ready for the con.

item.body:
[-][b][color=#ff5100]Price reduced.[/color][/b]
Ra ‐ 25th Century Games English deluxe edition (2023) Publisher: 25th Century Games
"Pharaoh edition" with wooden tiles and metal scoring tokens. Also includes the enamel Ra pin.
Verified complete. Lightly played and everything is pretty much pristine. No chipping on the images on the tiles. Box has very light wear, primarily a few small creases on one edge. Officially "very good" because it is opened and played.
Originally $95 (including shipping) from the Gamefound campaign. Asking [-]$80.00[/-] $70.00, cash at con.
I'm not sure I'll be selling enough to have a table at the VFM. I will be at the con Tuesday (for setup, I'm on Teem Geek) through Sunday and we can arrange a meetup.
[/-]Sold to [user=spurkster][/user] for $70.00.

item.body:
Huge Red Dragon Inn Bundle Price: Make an offer!
+remove+ Sales closed to prepare for the convention
I did...a thing. I bought Red Dragon Inn. Then I bought Red Dragon Inn 2. Then 3. Then the Character Trove box (aka Red Dragon Inn 5). Then I traded for someone to get the special Red Dragon Inn cards that came from another game. Then I bought promos. Then - and this is where the insanity begins - I sleeved it. Everything. The sleeved cards got so big that I bought a second copy of the Character Trove box. And even that was not enough, as I use the Smorgasbox for storing tokens and coins and stuff. There is a lot of Red Dragon Stuff here!
Here's what is included [thing=24310][/thing] [thing=33451][/thing] [thing=66510][/thing] [thing=142402][/thing] [thing=173634][/thing] (Two boxes, sold/traded the duplicate cards) [thing=46530][/thing] [thing=212662][/thing] [thing=244258][/thing] [thing=330097][/thing] [thing=273240][/thing] [thing=125472][/thing] [thing=302181][/thing] [thing=125053][/thing] [thing=146330][/thing] [thing=168857][/thing] [thing=146329][/thing] [thing=196213][/thing] [thing=233290][/thing] [thing=159683][/thing] [thing=249578][/thing] [thing=158222][/thing] [thing=286882][/thing] [thing=174922][/thing] [thing=173959][/thing] [thing=258289][/thing] [thing=370880][/thing] (I think I have some more promos but this is the only one I logged as part of my collection)
I wrote "make an offer" above because I am not sure what a collection of this size should go for. The entire collection is sleeved in FFG premium sleeves as well. So, if you have an interest, hit me up via Geek Mail or post a comment and we'll discuss. 😎
Edit: I should have predicted this and pre-emptively answered this question. I am not currently interested in splitting out parts of this collection. It's either staying with me or leaving my collection as a unit. That being said, I have seen folks in the past that use the comments to divvy up a listing such as this. As long as the entire collection goes, it can be split up amongst friends.
I will add the list of promos and extras that I have over the weekend for those that have asked for details about those.

[size=9][url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/342440?Seller=SwimmingScorpion&Status=NotSold]Click here to view all my items available for sale[/url][/size]
item.comment: I will offer you $5 for just the Andrea Smith promo materials if you want to dig it out. It's one of the few I don't yet have.
If nobody wants the lot then I might be willing to take that offer closer to the date of the con.

Okay, how about this. I will commit to the $40 so consider the entire lot committed (meaning I will pay the full $40 if needed). If you would then reset your listing to $35, and if someone else wants the bundle (which admittedly is an amazing bargain for all three of those games) then we've basically split the deal, otherwise I will pay the full $40 price. Is that something you're willing to do? Am I making sense?

That does make perfect sense. However, it's a lot more effort on my part than I really want to deal with. So, instead, either A) you buy the whole lot now and you can do what you want for the actual game and expansions once they're in your possession or B) if the lot hasn't sold by the week before the VFM, I'll get back to you and sell you the promo for the $5.
For now I will leave my offer at $5 for the promo. I have already picked up a copy of Dead of Winter during this VFM or I would simply take the entire bundle deal.

Darian, I have negotiated an alternate option to my prior Dead of Winter purchase, so I would now like to say I will take your bundle for your $40 asking price. Thanks for putting up with my waffling. :)
No problem. What's your preferred method of payment and do you want to pick up at the VFM or make alternate arrangements?
Darian, you can use this to pay for the Apiary bundle you bought from me. 🙂 So this plus $30 equals the $70 purchase price for Apiary.
Yeah, I was just updating my spreadsheet and caught that. Was going to message you the week before the con to work out final details just in case either of us got any more stuff from each other.

[q="swimmingscorpion"]Yeah, I was just updating my spreadsheet and caught that. Was going to message you the week before the con to work out final details just in case either of us got any more stuff from each other.[/q] That's fair! Will see how it works out. :)

To anyone following this item - I am only interested in some cards and bits from the core game (and the promo). The Warring Colonies and Long Night games will be available once I go through and sort / count everything. If you would be interested in picking these up after the VFM but before the convention is over, send me a Geek Mail to discuss. 🙂
If you are a fan of Dead of Winter one thing you might consider is offering me a few bucks for the Zombie standees. I found a super-cheap copy of DOW and added extra zombies to my original copy so I never had to use those silly little zombie button tokens for those (not so rare) occasions when you need more zombies. Also if you want extra dice, or if your game board is beat up. The only things I want from the base game are about 35 of the character cards that were unexpectedly missing from a special edition (TableTop exclusive cover) that I picked up at Half Price Books.

Thanks for the response! If it has minis and upgraded bits, its the Guildmaster. If so would you be open to a bundle sale of this and Veiled Fate for $110?

Ouch. These together are $200 and I just bumped them down for final sale to $70 and $80 which would be $150. I can't do $110... that's almost buy one get one free. Even together I think I gotta stick with $150. I priced all of my stuff a lot lower so I don't need to bring them into the bazaar but I can always sell them for going rate there. It's just a pain for me to bring them in a wagon to the event which is why I listed stuff here cheaper. If you're up for $150, they're yours.

Gotcha, and appreciate the response. No offense intended and understand your position. Offer was based around current VFM sales for Edge of Darkness and average rate for Veiled. Unfortunately I'll have to pass, best of luck, they are great games!

As an FYI, I have no issues with offers for less than my asking price. I only get annoyed when people try to justify these offers using the BGG marketplace, the list price from an online retailer or some other venue. [b]Comments:[/b] ➡️This auction is for a mystery box of games. ➡️Each bid must be in full dollar increments and larger than the prior bid. ➡️For each bid received, I will give a clue about the contents of the mystery box. ➡️Feel free to ask a question with your bid. The clue I provide [b]might[/b] answer the question asked. ➡️The auction will end at a time of my choosing on November 8.
[b]Clues:[/b] 1️⃣ The mystery box will include at least 4 games. 2️⃣ At least one of the games in the mystery box has a playmat for a board. 3️⃣ At least one of the games in the mystery box is a Legacy, Campaign game. From what I can tell, none of the legacy components have been used. 4️⃣ At least one of the games in the mystery box is a party game. 5️⃣ At least two of the games in the mystery box accommodate a player count of up to six players. 6️⃣ The designer of one of the games in the mystery box also designed another game that is ranked in the top 100 of [geekurl=/browse/boardgame]BGG[/geekurl]. 7️⃣ One of the two designers (different than clue 6) of one of the games in the mystery box also designed (in part or entirely) two games that are ranked in the top 200 of [geekurl=/browse/boardgame]BGG[/geekurl]. 8️⃣ At least one of the games is an abstract strategy game. 9️⃣ According to BGG, at least one of the games is best with 1 player. 🔟 According to BGG, at the time of this writing, the average ranking of at least four of the games in this bundle is 5.95. 1️⃣1️⃣ According to BGG, at the time of this writing, the average play time of at least four of the games in this bundle is 46.25 minutes. 1️⃣2️⃣ Of the minimum 4 games included in the mystery box, one was released in the 1990's, two were released in the aughts, and one was released in the teens. 1️⃣3️⃣ According to BGG, at the time of this writing, the game weight range of the games included in this bundle is from 1.30 to 4.15. 1️⃣4️⃣ The designer is also the artist of one of the games in the mystery box. 1️⃣5️⃣ Of the minimum 4 games included in the mystery box, two were published by one publisher (each different), one was published by four different publishers and one was published by five different publishers. 1️⃣6️⃣ None of the of the minimum 4 games included in the mystery box include someone's first name in the title, but one of the games does share the last name, although different spelling, of a (lesser-known?) celebrity chef. 1️⃣7️⃣ You may not have earned this title in your workplace, but if you find your way, you might be the initial sojourner to experience Ares' counterpart and that's no nonsense.
[b]Exchange notes:[/b] 1. Let's exchange at the meetup. 2. Cash, Zelle or PayPal accepted (in order of preference). If paying with PayPal please make sure to pay with Friends & Family.

item.body:
1973 Third Edition from The Avalon Hill Game Co. It's old and I am not the original owner. The box has dishing, corner splits, a little tape, and some grease pencil pricing. Board, chits, and rules are in great shape. I believe it's all there and don't recall missing pieces when I played. Nice 1970s Avalon Hill catalog also included.
Tactics II is an introductory war game with a basic and advanced game, plus optional rules to add flavor. I enjoyed it as a gaming history lesson and it's fun to see mechanics from it's time show up in more current games.
[b]Mechanics:[/b] Dice Rolling, Grid Movement, Movement Points, Simulation

2003 Fleer/Skybox. Complete and in great condition. I have 8 60 card starter decks (picked up at BGG,con, I think)
Sci-Fi gladiator fights using a mechanic called "The Flow". Each card has a "+" or "-" on it. Play a positively charged card, and you can keep playing cards. Play a negatively charged card and your turn ends and your opponent can start playing their cards. Basically, it helps provide a little "momentum" incentive, and adds strategy.
[b]Mechanics: [/b]Deck construction, Hand management

Up to the seller, but typically these go to the first person who commits to the asking price. Otherwise everyone could bid $1 and then have an option on every item. I know that’s the extreme, but still applies.

Go ahead, CJ. I'll retract my bid. 🙂
It's best to bid the asking price up front if you're willing to pay it, even if that means shelling out another $5 to $10. If you bid under, you run the risk of losing out to someone bidding the asking price.
Nah man, in reality you did state $80 first. I think its fair if you take it. You're 100% correct.

Item: Life of the Amazonia KS Deluxe with Wooden Waterfall Condition: Like New / New (see below)
+sold+ to [user=Joker3423] in a bundle deal
[-]I changed this listing to an auction. The starting bid is as shown, and the buy it now price takes everything immediately. The reserve means if the bidding does not meet or exceed that amount, I reserve (thus the name I guess) the right to not sell. I may also sell if the bid does not meet or exceed that amount depending on my mood, the phase of the moon, and how many other things I have bought at this VFM by then. 🙂 If you have any questions, please ask before you bid so I can clarify.
Description This is a bundle that includes everything produced for this game, including the extremely hard to find wooden waterfall upgrade kit. The game has been opened and played a few times and remains in Like New condition. Cards are sleeved with Gamegenic matte sleeves, which are premium (thicker) sleeves. I believe the matte sleeves are better than the transparent sleeves sold with the KS, but matte versus clear can be a matter of opinion. The wooden waterfall has never been assembled, and in fact is new in the original package. The animal meeples used for the game are stored in a plastic Plano-style (not a Plano brand in this case) tackle box. The animal meeples sold as extras are not in the box (they don't fit) but are still in the original accessory box. The original cardboard components are not stored in the box but are available. If you want them, let me know, otherwise the game will be delivered to you with just the premium / upgraded components.
[thing=368305][/thing] [thing=399281][/thing] [thing=399270][/thing] [thing=427449][/thing] [thing=427448][/thing] [thing=427450][/thing] (Doesn't add a thing to the game, just provides some replacement meeples should you want to display them. Or maybe you lost one of the originals) [thing=427447][/thing]
The Wooden Waterfall is probably the most compelling component of this collection, so I will go ahead and answer the question now...No, I am not interested in selling it separately. Those who know me (and those who read my VFM entries) probably get the idea that when I get a game I am an "All-In" type of person. That means I either buy (and keep) it all, or I sell it all as a bundle. I don't want to sell the waterfall and not sell the game and then regret not having it later. So...no splitting.

Item: Shadows Over Camelot + Sir Bedivere, the 8th Knight Condition: Like New Price: $90 +sold+ to [user=skalpol]
[-]Description This copy of Shadows Over Camelot has been counted and is 100% complete. All minis, cards, tokens, and so on are present. This copy also includes the promotional version the extra knight. Please note that the promotional version did not come with the custom orange die that was later provided in the Merlin expansion. This is the promotional knight that is included with this bundle.
[thing=20857][/thing]
One of the things I've noticed in trading this game is the edges of the white cards tend to go gray over time. It's one of the primary reasons I sleeve my games now. 🙂 [-]The cards in this copy are definitely a bit gray around the edges but no other defects were noted.[/-] After reviewing this copy again I am going to retract that last statement. The cards - when compared to a set of Merlin cards from my other copy that have not been played - look quite good.
Here's a picture of the cards fanned out [imageid=8465202 medium]
Here's a picture of the edges compared with a set of cards from an un-played Merlin deck (note that Merlin is [b]not[/b] included in this listing, I just pulled the cards from another copy of the game). You can sort of tell where the base deck ends and the Merlin deck begins, but barely. [imageid=8465204 medium]
The plastic trays for the catapults, knights, and so on are still included in this game (sometimes owners toss those and just leave the minis loose in the insert). The manuals look fantastic with no creases or bends. The game box has extremely minor shelf wear. For these reasons I don't have a problem classifying this copy as "like new." As with all my used games, if upon inspection you are not satisfied with my condition rating you are free to cancel the sale.

item.body:
Item: Shadows Over Camelot + Merlin's Company Condition: See Below Price: $250
+remove+ Sales closed to prepare for convention
Description Merlin's Company has been combined into the base game and the original expansion box is no longer available. The expansion has not been played, but the white card pack has been opened. The black card pack is still in shrink.
Because the base game has been played, the edges of the white cards are clearly "dirtier" than the brand new cards from the expansion. Sleeving the cards should eliminate the ability to see which cards are clean versus dirty. If you hold up the decks (used vs. unused) you can clearly tell which cards come from the expansion right now. Sleeve your games, people! 😛
Here is a picture showing the edges of the base deck compared with the cleaner (un-played) Merlin deck. [imageid=8465203 medium] I believe sleeving these cards would eliminate this edge issue.
The trays for the miniatures have been discarded, and the miniatures are stored in zip lock baggies instead. Nothing has been painted. The minis for Merlin and Sir Bedivere are in separate blister packs rather than the zip lock baggies.
All of the dice are present, including the orange die for Sir Bedivere as provided by the Merlin expansion. The base game comes with 8 knight cards. Merlin adds 7 more (doubling up on all of the knights except King Arthur) to provide more variety in player powers. Merlin also adds, well, Merlin. 🙂 Merlin has a travel deck that impacts the knights as they attempt to travel from station to station.
The game box looks fantastic for something of its age. The game manuals have very, very slight imperfections. Enough so that I am not going to use the Like New condition, but maybe call it Very Good +++.

Item: Shadows Over Camelot + Merlin's Company Condition: See Below Price: $275
+remove+ Sales closed to prepare for convention
Description Yes, this is my third copy of Shadows Over Camelot for this VFM. 🙂 This one, however, not only includes the expansion but also the expansion box! And yes, the cards are (finally!) sleeved! It's a beautifully preserved copy of this decade+ old game. The base game box currently has the base game (sleeved cards), miniatures in their expected trays, and the dice. The previous owner was also nice enough to include a couple of fabric straps that make lifting the card decks out of the wells very easy. The manuals look brand new. The base game box has very, very minimal wear.
The Merlin's Company box has some extremely light dishing. I probably would not notice it but for my asking price I feel I owe it to the potential buyer to disclose anything / everything that would bother me about the game. So there's that. The white deck for Merlin has been opened, but never played. The black deck for Merlin is still shrink wrapped. The additional knights and the Merlin manual round out what's stored in the Merlin box.

If I do not qualify for a seller table I will be flexible as to when to meet for an exchange. :arrowE: I accept PayPal Friends and Family once you have had the opportunity to inspect your purchase. item.body:
2012 Matagot edition. Complete with box, miniatures, and other components in great condition.
Another classic! Play as a god from Egyptian mythology, bringing forth your armies of followers and creatures you recruit to control the upper Nile and delta. Masterful implementation of emergent asymmetry in the game design with all gods starting the same and recruiting unique combinations of abilities and creatures from a common pool. This one still holds up (even compared to Kemet: Blood & Sand) and has fantastic art, styled like a 70s album cover airbrushed on the side of panel van. Only selling because I have another copy.
[b]Mechanics: [/b]Area Majority, Card play conflict resolution, Open drafting, Tech trees

item.comment: You mentioned NIS, so am I right in guessing this doesn't have the 3 corrected cards?

[q="gericke"]You mentioned NIS, so am I right in guessing this doesn't have the 3 corrected cards?[/q]
Not sure.
NOTE: The 2022 Kickstarter for Final Girl: Season 2 included a 13 card Final Girl: First Printing Correction Pack of corrected cards for the first printing of Final Girl: Series 1. The cards mostly fix typos and are not required to play the game. The cards were corrected for the second printing of Final Girl: Series 1.
This could be the second printing, but unsure.
I will offer $20 for Final Girl + Happy Trails.
[q="gericke"]I will offer $20 for Final Girl + Happy Trails.[/q] Yeah we can do that. Marking sold to you!

item.comment: I'll take Life of the Amazonia for $40
[q="MJPrudhomme"]I'll take Life of the Amazonia for $40[/q] Sorry about that. Ended up selling this in a bundle locally.

Lance, can you tag your item +remove+ so it doesn't show up as available on the search index anymore, since it's not available? It's not a requirement, of course, but it's convenient for those that rely on the list content. :)

[q="drathbun"]Lance, can you tag your item +remove+ so it doesn't show up as available on the search index anymore, since it's not available? It's not a requirement, of course, but it's convenient for those that rely on the list content. :)[/q] Ah my apologies. So putting Sold inside the post doesn't remove it from your tool is that correct? The other tool removes it from the search index.

For me, yes. 🙂 There is a difference between "sold" and "remove" actually. Sold means that it was sold on the VFM. If something was listed on the VFM and then sold elsewhere, or perhaps lost, or the seller simply changed their mind, then the +remove+ tag removes it from the list entirely. It's like it never existed...the item will not show up as available, or sold, or anything.
The link at the bottom of your post goes to "Unsold" items, and yes, it's removed from there. But if you look at the list overall, this item still shows up. I don't know if YulGames supports the +remove+ tag or not, but my index definitely does. To my way of thinking this is more appropriate, as the "sold items" are used to assign tables for the VFM, and items sold outside of the VFM should not be counted towards that list. Anyway, probably more detail than you wanted, but that's the reason for my suggestion. :)

Seller backed out on the sale. 😞

Matt,
I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to personally apologize for backing out of our board game transaction. I understand how frustrating and disappointing it must be to think you’ve secured something, only for it to fall through unexpectedly. I deeply regret taking up your time and putting you through that emotional rollercoaster.
Looking back, I recognize that I could have communicated more effectively and much sooner, and I’m genuinely sorry for not doing so. I understand that a simple delay or lack of clarity can lead to unnecessary frustration, and I take full responsibility for not validating the sale before listing the item. I can assure you that I will take extra care in the future to double-check all details before committing to anything, so this doesn’t happen again.
Please accept my sincerest apologies once more for any inconvenience caused, and thank you for your understanding. I truly appreciate your patience and hope that despite this situation, you will consider shopping with me again in the future.

Item: Dinosaur Island + Expansion + Broken Token Insert Bundle Condition: Like New, See below for exceptions Starting Bid: $50 Buy It Now: $80 Auction End: Saturday Nov. 9
Auction ended - no bids
+remove+ Sales closed to prepare for the convention
Description Tis is the deluxe edition for the base game and for the expansion and it has the Broken Token inserts for both. The inserts are designed to consolidate the expansion into the base game box so there is no expansion box, and there is a fairly substantial amount of lid lift (about 2" just eye-balling it). The box looks to be in great shape. After carefully sorting and counting everything, the bundle is complete except for the metal coins that should be in the deluxe version of the base game. See below for options.
[thing=221194][/thing] Deluxe, missing metal coins, all other components accounted for [thing=248591][/thing] Deluxe, complete [thing=285323][/thing] ($53 from BT) [thing=285324][/thing] ($42 from BT)
I have sorted and counted everything. There are a few confusing bits. For example, the Liquid expansion book says there should be five executive pawns...there are not. There are instead 8 yellow custom figures for each executive position. This was discussed [article=30672184]here[/article]. [b]The only thing missing that is expected to be there is the set of metal coins.[/b] The expected number of cardboard money tokens are there. But with the Broken Token inserts I am still comfortable with my $50 opening bid.
If you are not interested in the Broken Token insert, I will reduce the cost by $25. That means if your final bid is $65 but you don't want the insert, you can pay $40 and I will keep the insert for my own copy of the game. Please keep in mind that all components will be consolidated into the base game box (no expansion box is available). If you [b]only[/b] want the insert, I will wait until someone bids / buys the game and then you can discuss that with them.
If you are bummed by the lack of the metal coins, I have an extra set of the Dinosaur World metal coins that I can include for $25. I have had these goon eBay for $50 so that's a substantial discount. I think the Dinosaur World coins are by far the better product anyway as far as their design. That means if your winning bid is $65 and you don't want the BT insert but you do want the alternate coins...carry the one...your final price is back to $65. 🙂
Please let me know if you have any questions!
